settings.title: Is a Ductless Mini-Split Right for Your Home?

settings.editor: A ductless mini-split may be a good fit if your current HVAC system does not keep certain rooms comfortable or if adding ductwork would be expensive or disruptive.
Ductless systems are especially helpful when you do not need to replace your entire HVAC system but still want better comfort in a specific area.

settings.title: Ductless Mini-Split Questions? We Have Answers

tabs.tab_title: How much does ductless mini-split installation cost in the Tri-Cities?
tabs.tab_content: Cost depends on the number of zones, system size, equipment selected, and installation complexity. Air Comfort Services provides upfront pricing before work begins.

tabs.tab_title: Can a ductless mini-split heat and cool my home?
tabs.tab_content: Yes. Many mini-split systems provide both heating and cooling, making them a flexible year-round comfort option.

tabs.tab_title: Is a ductless mini-split better than central AC?
tabs.tab_content: It depends on your home. Central AC is often best for whole-home cooling when ductwork is in place. Ductless mini-splits are ideal for room-by-room comfort, additions, older homes, and spaces without ducts.

tabs.tab_title: How often should ductless mini-splits be serviced?
tabs.tab_content: Most systems should be serviced at least once per year. Systems used for both heating and cooling may benefit from maintenance twice per year.

tabs.tab_title: Do ductless mini-splits use less energy?
tabs.tab_content: They can be efficient because they heat and cool specific zones instead of conditioning the entire home at once. Savings depend on system size, usage, insulation, and maintenance.

tabs.tab_title: Why is my ductless mini-split leaking water?
tabs.tab_content: A leaking mini-split may have a clogged condensate drain, dirty indoor coil, drainage issue, or installation problem. Service can help prevent water damage and performance issues.
